Easter ’67 poster

Ian McLaren’s poster for the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament’s Easter 1967 march: a field of white dots on black that swell into a glowing disc under a plain grotesque headline.

Source
V&A: Poster “Easter ’67”, E.383-2021
Creator
Ian McLaren (artist); Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament (issuer)
Made
1967
Style
Op art (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
High-contrast, urgent, radiant
Evidence
Downloaded and inspected the V&A photograph of its copy, E.383-2021 (1110 × 1600 px), photographed on a wooden surface, in a scratchpad. No image is stored.

28 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The V&A catalogues the poster with the style “Op Art”, gives Ian McLaren as artist and the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament (CND) as issuer, and dates it 1967. V&A.

The V&A record has no further description. The event text on the poster lists Easter Saturday at Grosvenor Square, Easter Sunday at Ruislip, and an Easter Monday march to a rally in Trafalgar Square.

Observed

  • The upper third is a solid black band with the CND symbol in a white disc and “Easter ’67” in large white grotesque capitals and lower case.
  • Four columns of small white sans-serif text give the organiser’s address and the times and places of the events.
  • The lower two thirds hold a square field of white dots on black. The dots are small at the edges and grow until they merge near the centre, so a bright, soft-edged disc appears.
  • The dot field seems to bulge toward the viewer. There is no colour.

Why it belongs

The poster follows the op rules for type and pattern: the text sits on solid black, apart from the field, and the field does the expressive work.

The swelling dot field can be read as a light or a blast, which gives the abstract device a message without adding a figure.

Borrow

Scale a regular dot grid so that the dots grow toward a centre and merge into a bright disc.

Keep all text in a separate solid band above the pattern, set in one plain grotesque at two sizes.
